name: Non-infectious Posterior Uveitis

criteria.description: Presence of inflammation localized to the posterior segment of the uvea (choroid, retina, or optic nerve head) without evidence of infectious etiology
Exclusion of infectious causes by laboratory testing and clinical evaluation
Chronic or recurrent inflammation lasting more than 3 months
Imaging findings consistent with posterior segment inflammation such as retinal vasculitis or choroiditis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of posterior segment inflammation with exclusion of infectious causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of infectious and masquerade syndromes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Vitritis (inflammatory cells in the vitreous humor)

common.notes: Perception of spots or threads in vision
Visual disturbance due to retinal irritation
Usually less severe than in anterior uveitis

occasional.notes: Inflammation of the optic nerve head
Mild anterior segment inflammation may be present
searchTerms: inflammatory cells in front eye chamber
white blood cells in anterior chamber

rare.notes: Elevated intraocular pressure due to inflammation
Secondary to chronic inflammation or corticosteroid therapy

laboratory: Negative infectious disease panels (e.g., syphilis, tuberculosis, toxoplasmosis)
Elevated inflammatory markers (e.g., ESR, CRP) in some cases
Autoimmune serologies may be positive if associated systemic disease present
imaging: Fluorescein angiography showing retinal vasculitis and leakage
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating macular edema
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible association with HLA types in some autoimmune cases
other: Clinical exclusion of infectious and neoplastic causes
Response to immunosuppressive therapy supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of response to immunosuppressive therapy

redFlags: Presence of hypopyon or severe anterior segment inflammation
Signs of systemic infection or malignancy
references: Jabs DA, Nussenblatt RB, Rosenbaum JT. Standardization of Uveitis Nomenclature for Reporting Clinical Data. Am J Ophthalmol. 2005;140(3):509-516.
Rothova A. Causes and prognosis of uveitis in the Netherlands. Br J Ophthalmol. 1996;80(4):332-336.
Nussenblatt RB. The natural history of uveitis. Int Ophthalmol. 1990;14(5-6):303-308.
